IncidentBot: PAGER — Novara VPC: KV prefix cache hit-rate collapse detected for tenant=novara. Symptoms: p99 token latency spike, increasing 504s on text-generation routes using cust:novara/* prefixes. Auto-escalating to eng-sre and eng-runtime. @Ash K @Sanjay Patel @Marta Reyes

Ash K: oncall acked. woke up, looking now. any quick summary of which prefixes are worst?

Lee Chen: quick query shows a dramatic hit-rate drop on prefixes matching cust:novara/core and cust:novara/rerank. Sample from metrics (1m window):
```
kv_prefix_hits{tenant="novara",prefix="cust:novara/core"} 12
kv_prefix_requests{tenant="novara",prefix="cust:novara/core"} 1200
kv_prefix_hitrate 0.01
eviction_rate 3400
memory_pressure 0.92
```
Eviction rate spiked ~09:12 UTC, correlates with a large batch reranker job we saw yesterday.

Sanjay Patel: Checking runtime logs — looks like auto-cache-disable triggered on nodes n-vpc-3a/n-vpc-3b due to compaction/memory guard. Those nodes disabled prefix caching for tenants above 8GB to protect stability. That caused fallthrough to backend and the hit-rate collapse.

Marta Reyes: Novara is running a high-fanout reranker that touches many long prefixes; classic cache pollution. Customer claims they started a nightly backfill at 08:50 UTC. We need immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle the Novara job, 2) increase per-tenant cache quota temporarily, 3) route Novara to a reserved pool, 4) prewarm critical prefixes.

Novara Ops: We're seeing transaction failures on merchant checkout flows — we need ETA. Customers are getting intermittent 504s and degraded latencies. Any safe quick fix?

Ash K: Short-term plan: 1) throttle Novara rerank traffic at the edge (rate limit heavy endpoints) 2) bump per-tenant cache quota on affected nodes to reduce auto-disable 3) prewarm core prefixes to recover hot set. I'll start 1 & 2 now.

Sanjay Patel: Executing throttles and quota bump in staged rollout. Commands I'm running:
```
# throttle heavy endpoints for novara
redwood route update --tenant novara --route "/v1/rerank" --rate-limit 0.2

# bump per-tenant cache quota for 30m
infractl kv-set-quota novara 12G --ttl 30m --regions us-west-1,us-east-1
```
Applying to us-west-1 first.

Lee Chen: Also starting a prewarm for the most-critical prefixes once quota is up:
```
kvctl prewarm --tenant novara --prefix "cust:novara/core" --limit 5000 --concurrency 4
```
This should rebuild the hot-key set and reduce backend calls.

PagerDuty: oncall handover in ~20m — current assignee @Ash K will hand to @Marta Reyes. Please confirm if you can take a 1hr follow-up.

Novara Ops: Appreciate the quick actions. Please keep us posted. We can throttle the backfill job from our side if that helps — will coordinate with our infra team.

Marta Reyes: I'll stay on the incident after handover. Follow-up items I'm logging: postmortem with root cause (auto-cache-disable thresholds too aggressive for bursty tenant workloads), change autoscaling/compaction heuristics to consider tenant isolation, add alarm for rapid eviction spikes per-tenant, and add a per-tenant prefetch/quota exemption flow for enterprise customers.

eng-runtime: Noting a short-term config change to lower the compaction sensitivity for the dedicated-pool nodes taking Novara traffic. We'll revert after traffic normalizes. Also recommend adding a safeguard to avoid global cache-disable for multi-tenant nodes — prefer per-tenant fallback.

Ash K: Update 09:28 UTC — throttle applied in us-west-1, quota bumped. Initial metrics show hit-rate climbing from 0.01 -> 0.18 for core prefixes; backend 504 rate down ~60% in region. Rolling to us-east-1 now.

IncidentBot: STATUS -> Mitigation in progress. Customer impact: reduced but still present for some edge flows. Next update in 15m or on major change. Pager duty note: handover to @Marta Reyes at 09:45 UTC.

Sanjay Patel: After stabilization we should schedule a short change with Novara: either dedicated pool or tuned cache-exemption policy. I'll start a support-runbook draft and ping Solutions.

Novara Ops: Thanks team. We'll remain on-call for customer communication. Please include any temporary mitigations in the ticket so we can update customers.

Marta Reyes: Affirmative. I'll collect logs, metrics graphs, and the mitigations list for the postmortem. Will also add an action to add pre-deploy job detectors for large fanout backfills.

Ash K: Handing to @Marta Reyes for post-handoff. Leaving heartbeat checks and a small watch script in the channel.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT NOTE appended: mitigation_actions=[throttle,routing-change,quota-bump,prewarm], customer_impacted=true, severity=high, followup_owner=Marta Reyes
